lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: conditional probability and its definition

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: Group X: 12 successes, 8 failures. Find P(success | X).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 5/10, P(B) = 1/10, and P(A and B) = 10/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

items.prompt: In a group of 32, 14 do activity A, 12 do activity B, and 2 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 1/8 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 13 successes and 9 failures; group Y with 23 successes and 18 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 6/10, P(B) = 2/10, and P(A and B) = 12/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a group of 25, 14 do activity A, 9 do activity B, and 5 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 1/7 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 5 successes and 42 failures; group Y with 26 successes and 33 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 6/10, P(B) = 7/10, and P(A and B) = 43/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.

items.prompt: In a group of 30, 17 do activity A, 11 do activity B, and 7 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
